data.narrative:
Teradar is a Series B defense and security technology company founded by MIT-trained leadership (CEO Matt Carey) and deep technical expertise in terahertz sensing (CTO Gregory Charvat, former Humatics CTO; Chief Chip Architect Nick Saiz). The company has raised $175M to date. The relevant peer set comprises 10 comparable companies across Defense & Security at similar stages: 2 public comps (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private companies, including Dream Security ($3.0B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Code Metal ($1.2B), Castelion ($1.0B), and Defense Unicorns ($1.0B).

Two valuation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy and applying a typical 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier, implies $332M. Peer-median analysis across the 7 same-sector, same-stage private comparables yields a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range of $300M to $3.0B, reflecting substantial variance in the peer universe.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $283M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $666M. The wide spread reflects genuine uncertainty about whether Teradar's technical differentiation and team quality command premium valuation versus the median peer, or whether earlier-stage financial performance justifies a below-peer entry. Key uncertainties include revenue traction, customer concentration in defense procurement, and execution risk on terahertz IC commercialization.
